correctness.rationale: A(y)=(B+y²)/(1+y²)>0 makes (x,y)→(U,y) globally invertible. The real inverse problem is exactly φ_U(y)=V, with φ_U'=1+2Ua y/(B+y²)² and φ_U(y)→±∞ at the two ends. The function r/(B+r²)² has unique maximum at √(B/3), of size 9/(16√3 B^(3/2)); this proves the threshold, strict monotonicity even at equality, and the +,−,+ derivative pattern outside it. At a cusp Ua=−(B+y²)²/(2y), y²=B/3, hence V=U+3y. The third derivative is 9/(2B) and the mixed derivative ∂_Uφ_U' is −1/U, so the cusp is ordinary and the inverse cubic has a triple root. Away from these points the critical roots are simple and give ordinary folds. Writing δ=ε/U_* and η=y−y_* yields the nonconstant terms −δη+3η³/(4B)+O_a(εη²+|η|⁴). At its extrema η=±(2/3)√(Bδ)+O_a(ε), the leading values differ by (8/9)√B δ^(3/2); the errors are O_a(ε²). The original determinant is Aφ_U', and bounded X bounds x, then bounded Y bounds y. The unique regular preimage at U=0 has positive sign, establishing degree +1. The a=0 affine limit is correct.
residual_risks: This is a one-step classification only, in the stated real parameter regime; finite supplementary tests are not proof.

value.rationale: The model is a published rational dynamical system and its first inverse valence is a basic input to backward dynamics. This locates all changes in that valence and quantifies the physical onset of multivalued inversion. It distinguishes the positivity-stratum geometry from the connected-strip and pinch geometry of the same model outside the regime, rather than just reasserting the universal cusp normal form.
residual_risks: No claim about forward attractors follows from the inverse census alone.
